description: 2nd-generation Kia Niro Hybrid (SG2, 2023+). 1.6L Smartstream Kappa II GDI engine paired with a 32 kW PMSM motor sandwiched in a 6-speed DCT, fed by a Li-Po HV pack. Parallel hybrid architecture (motor in transmission), unlike Toyota HSD planetary split. Mode 21 is dead everywhere; all live data comes via Mode 22 (UDS) — and only after entering the extended diagnostic session (UDS 10 03), which the web Sampler and the sweep tool both handle automatically. Two distinct data namespaces: (1) BMS at 7E4 owns the 0x01xx DID space with HV-pack telemetry (SOC, cell temps, cell voltages, charge current); (2) Engine ECU at 7E0 owns the 0xF4xx DID space, where Kia transplanted every standard SAE J1979 Mode 01 PID — F4<pid> on engine ECU returns the same payload the standard 01<pid> would on a normal car. The 4 emissions-mandated PIDs (01, 21, 30, 31) are also kept on the standard Mode 01 path for regulatory reasons. This profile decodes 9 BMS signals and ~36 engine telemetry signals (rpm, speed, throttle, MAF, coolant, fuel, O2 sensors, catalyst temps, etc.) via that Mode 22 0xF4xx mirror.
sources: Empirical sweeps + raw captures against a 2026 Kia Niro LX Hybrid rental on 2026-06-14. Sweep that surfaced the 19 BMS DIDs with multi-frame assembled: sweep__2026-06-14T13-42-49Z.json. BMS decode source: raw__2026-06-14T14-15-57Z__bxh8q530.csv (76 ticks, RPM range 0-9269, varied throttle / engine load, coolant climbing 122-132°F).

Engine telemetry F4xx discovery: sweep__2026-06-14T16-17-32Z.json found 56 responsive DIDs on the engine ECU at 7E0 in the Mode 22 0xF4xx range. The lower-nibble pattern matched standard SAE J1979 Mode 01 PIDs 1:1 (F40C = RPM, F40D = speed, F411 = throttle position, etc.) with identical byte layouts and identical decode formulas. Empirical validation against the sweep snapshot: F40C = 2A 6C → 2715 RPM (ICE was active during sweep), F405 = 77 → 79°C coolant, F410 = 02 8A → 6.50 g/s MAF, F442 = 35 2D → 13.61V 12V battery, F4A6 = 04 00 00 0D → odometer.

BMS ECU address (7E4) and Mode 22 0x01xx DID space cross-checked against community Hyundai-Kia hybrid sources: EV Notify project, Torque Pro Kia/Hyundai DID database, HybridKia and Niro forums. The F4xx engine mirror is empirically identified here; not yet found in community sources.

validated_against.notes:
Two refinements after a 98-minute / 70-mile real-world drive (2026-06-14T16:50:30Z__799tbz3t.csv) surfaced two artifacts:

(1) inverter_coolant_temp reported a constant 250-255°C across a 10-minute follow-up session when the inverter was thermally quiesced. Byte 19 of DID 0107 was returning 0xFA-0xFF — the SAE J1979 sentinel for 'sensor unavailable / no data'. The earlier active-driving capture showed real values (82-164°C), so byte 19 is the correct byte for inverter temp. Now wrapped in nullIfGte(T, 254) — the formula evaluator returns NaN for sentinel readings and pid-codec maps NaN to a blank CSV cell instead of writing literal '255'.

(2) hv_charge_current peaked at 654.4 A during the long drive — physically impossible (Niro Hybrid regen peaks around 50 kW = ~210 A at the pack's ~240V nominal). Hypothesis: bytes 55-56 of DID 0101 are a 16-bit signed two's-complement value (positive = charging into pack, negative = discharging from pack). 0xFFAB unsigned = 65,451 / 100 = 654.51 A; signed = -85 / 100 = -0.85 A regen flow. Normal positive charging values (0-150 A) are unaffected — for 16-bit values below 32768 the signed and unsigned interpretations are identical. Renamed to hv_pack_current with sign convention documented in display_name. CSV column name change is breaking for any pandas script keyed on 'hv_charge_current'.

Tool changes shipped alongside this profile:
  - src/obd/formula.ts + iOS FormulaEvaluator.swift: added signed16(n) and nullIfGte(value, threshold) helpers. iOS wrapper also gains min/max/abs/signed aliases for parity (those were missing from iOS but present in web FUNCTIONS).
  - src/obd/pid-codec.ts: NaN / Infinity from evaluateFormula now treated as 'no data' (blank cell), enabling nullIfGte to work end-to-end.

Known limitations of 0.4.0:
  - The signed16 hypothesis for hv_pack_current is plausible but not directly verified against raw bytes from the 654 A spike ticks (the drive was in decoded mode). If a follow-up raw capture shows different byte patterns at regen, the formula may need revision. Bias is safe: normal positive readings unchanged; previously-impossible high readings now read as small negative regen flows.

Referenced captures: raw__2026-06-14T14-15-57Z__bxh8q530.csv (76 ticks, BMS decode source), 2026-06-14T16-50-30Z__799tbz3t.csv (98 min, full F4xx + BMS coverage), 2026-06-14T20-22-27Z__dzqxhbj5.csv (10 min, surfaced the inverter sentinel).

Continuation of the BMS work documented below. After the 0.2.0 ship, noticed the engine ECU (7E0) was reporting only 4 PIDs on standard Mode 01 (01, 21, 30, 31 — the emissions-mandated set) even with the ICE running and clearly producing power (HV charge current peaked at 71 A in the BMS readout). Hypothesis: Kia gates engine telemetry behind extended diagnostic session at the engine ECU too, parallel to the BMS gating we'd already worked around. Probed Mode 22 ranges 0xF400-0xF4FF, 0xC000-0xC0FF, 0x4400-0x44FF in extended session. 0xF4xx returned 56 OK responses on engine ECU; the other ranges returned NRC 31 across all 5 ECUs. The F4xx lower-nibble pattern matched standard Mode 01 PIDs 1:1 — Kia transplanted the entire Mode 01 surface to Mode 22 0xF4<pid>, retaining standard Mode 01 only for the 4 emissions-required PIDs. Validated sweep response payloads against standard SAE J1979 formulas: F40C = 0x2A6C → (0x2A*256+0x6C)/4 = 2715 RPM (consistent with HV charging RPM), F405 = 0x77 → 0x77-40 = 79°C (warm engine), F410 = 0x028A → 6.50 g/s MAF (idle-ish), F411 = 0x2B → 16.86% throttle, F442 = 0x352D → 13.613V 12V battery (normal). All formulas decoded to physically sensible values. Profile now adds 36 engine telemetry PIDs at Mode 22 F4xx (rpm, speed, throttle, MAF, engine_load, coolant_temp, fuel_rate, all O2/cat-temp/fuel-trim/EGR/evap, and odometer). PID IDs deliberately match `STANDARD_MODE_01` in src/obd/standard-pids.ts so that on a normal car these would dedupe against auto-discovered standards (registry-builder dedupe by id) — on the Niro, the standard auto-discovery doesn't find them and the F4xx profile entry wins. The 4 PIDs that ARE auto-discovered as standard (monitor_status, distance_with_mil, warmups_since_clear, distance_since_clear) are intentionally NOT redeclared in the profile; they continue to flow through standard Mode 01. Tool changes shipped earlier (1003 entry, multi-frame reassembly, formula evaluator A-Z + byte()) are reused unchanged.

Validated_against (BMS work, retained from v0.2.0):

Workflow: (1) Confirmed Mode 21 dead everywhere on this car (NRC 11 across all 256 PIDs at engine/MCU/VCU/BMS/HCU). (2) Mode 22 also returned NRC 31 across 0x0000-0x00FF, 0x0100-0x01FF, 0x0200-0x02FF, 0x0500-0x05FF, 0x4000-0x40FF, 0xB000-0xB0FF in default diagnostic session — strong signature of session gating. (3) F1xx identification DIDs returned 48 OK responses including F190 (VIN start) and F197 = 'BMS' on 7E4, confirming Mode 22 is supported and the BMS lives at 7E4 as the EV community suggests. (4) Adding UDS 10 03 (extendedDiagnosticSession) entry before Mode 22 sweep unlocked 19 BMS DIDs in 0x0101-0x01F2 range. (5) After fixing multi-frame ISO-TP reassembly in the sweep + sampler, full payloads (45-122 bytes per DID) flowed through to raw-mode CSVs. (6) Byte-slice correlation against rpm / engine_load / throttle / speed / coolant_temp across 76 ticks identified the 9 named signals shipping in this profile.

IDENTIFICATIONS:
  - soc_display (0101 byte 4): range 84-103 raw = 42.0-51.5% SOC. Weak state correlations (expected — SOC drifts slowly). E/2 matches Hyundai-Kia EV BMS convention.
  - cell_temp_1..4 (0101 bytes 14-17, formulas O,P,Q,R): range 30-33°C raw. Pearson +0.68 to +0.78 vs coolant_temp — consistent with cells sharing the engine cooling loop on this generation. Same 4-byte pattern as the Lexus RX 450h PID 95.
  - cell_v_max (0101 byte 23 = X): range 172-190 raw → 3.44-3.80V at 0.02V/LSB. Matches per-cell voltages observed in DID 0102/0103.
  - cell_v_min (0101 byte 25 = Z): range 171-190 raw → 3.42-3.80V. Same scale as max.
  - hv_charge_current (0101 bytes 55-56): range 0-5754 raw → 0-57.5A unsigned. Pearson +0.873 vs rpm, +0.830 vs maf, +0.810 vs engine_load — by far the strongest correlation of any byte in any DID. Goes up when ICE works harder, consistent with engine-driven generator charging the HV pack. NOTE: this is the CHARGE side; the discharge / regen side may live at adjacent bytes or in a separate DID — not yet identified.
  - inverter_coolant_temp (0107 byte 19 = T): range 19-20°C raw. Pearson +0.88 vs coolant_temp — almost certainly an inverter / power-electronics coolant inlet temp.

UNRESOLVED / RETAINED AS RAW:
  - 0102 + 0103 carry 32 + 32 = 64 cell voltages (each byte = one cell, *0.02V). Decoding into 64 individual cell PIDs would explode the column count; deferred. The raw payloads are in the CSV.
  - 0107 has strong-correlation bytes at offsets 4, 6, 8, 10-13, 23, 42 that look like temperatures, motor signals, or counters. Need more varied-state captures (especially regen + EV-only) to disambiguate.
  - 0108 has 26 distinct payloads — multiple state-dependent bytes. Charging power, energy throughput, or fault flags suspected.
  - 0114 (22 bytes, 4 distinct payloads) and 0130-0134 (44-75 bytes each, mostly static during this drive) likely contain energy / odometer-style counters that didn't move much in ~2 minutes of driving.
  - 01F2 (122 bytes, 6 distinct payloads) is the biggest single DID — likely a full system state block worth dedicated identification effort.

WHAT'S MISSING:
  - HV pack voltage: standard Mode 01 PID 5C (hv_system_voltage) is supported on this Niro and is auto-discovered, so a custom PID isn't needed.
  - HV pack discharge current / regen current: not yet found. May be in 0101 bytes 24-26 (range 1-40, 171-190, 1-56 — weak state correlations) or in another DID. Worth a follow-up with explicit regen-braking captures.
  - Motor torque, motor RPM, gear engaged: 7E2 and 7E3 are alive ECUs that returned NRC 31 across 0x0100-0x01FF in extended session — they have Mode 22 DIDs somewhere but we haven't found the range. Kia likely keeps motor data behind their K-DS dealer tooling with authenticated sessions; this may not be reachable with standard tools.

TOOL CHANGES SHIPPED ALONGSIDE THIS PROFILE:
  - src/obd/sweep.ts + samplers: send UDS 10 03 before Mode 22 queries when any Mode 22 PID is grouped at an ECU.
  - src/obd/sweep.ts + src/obd/pid-codec.ts + iOS Sampler.swift: assemble multi-frame ISO-TP responses into one payload, strip the response prefix, trim AA padding.
  - src/obd/formula.ts + iOS FormulaEvaluator.swift: extended byte variables from A-H/A-J to A-Z and added byte(n) for indices ≥26, so formulas can reach the deeper offsets in long Mode 22 payloads.
